title: Observation stream, version 1
description: What a debugger adapter emits, before any interpretation. The adapter reports what it saw: it assigns no identity, detects no sharing, and computes no delta. See docs/OBSERVATION-SPEC.md and docs/decisions/ADR-003.

detail.description: The named reason, when termination is not Completed.

max_reads.description: The largest single read the adapter performed, per kind. Instrumentation for SPEC-TEST-020: 'no read exceeded the bound' is asserted by what was read, not by the absence of a crash.

value_state.description: 0 Valid, 1 Not_Yet_Active, 2 Unreadable, 3 Unknown. Four states, never three: 'not created yet', 'I could not read it', and 'I read it and it makes no sense' point a student at different bugs. See ADR-008.

kind.description: 0 Scalar, 1 String, 2 Slice, 3 Dynamic_Array, 4 Fixed_Array, 5 Struct, 6 Pointer, 7 Map, 8 Opaque.

termination.description: 0 Completed, 1 Limit_Steps, 2 Limit_Wall_Time, 3 Target_Crashed, 4 Target_Became_Multithreaded, 5 Debug_Info_Missing, 6 Adapter_Failed.

budgets.description: What the adapter declares it enforced. The core cannot verify a budget enforced at the read, so it compares this declaration with its own configuration. An adapter that lies is not detectable; that is the accepted price of enforcing read budgets at the read. See ADR-006.

address.description: Address of the value itself. Used only to derive identity; it never reaches the trace. See SPEC-MEM-001.

elem_size.description: Bytes per element. The core needs it to decide whether two views overlap, which is how a sub-slice is recognised as a window onto its parent's buffer.

reason.description: Why the state is not Valid. Required in practice for every non-Valid state: 'unknown' with no cause teaches nothing.

caller_pc.description: The CALLER's program counter. Two calls on one source line are two call sites and therefore two return addresses, which is what tells sibling invocations apart. See SPEC-MEM-060.

returned.description: A value attributed to the invocation that produced it, by frame key. When attribution fails the adapter emits nothing rather than guessing. See SPEC-MEM-061.

stdout_len.description: Cumulative BYTES of the target's output at this stop. Bytes, not characters: the unit is in the name because a prior system lost whole documents to a character count guarding a byte limit. See SPEC-SAFE-031.

objects.description: Objects reached by following pointers at this step, breadth-first and bounded by both expansion budgets. A flat list, not nested inside the pointer that found it: a cycle cannot be nested. See SPEC-MEM-030.

address.description: Where the object lives. The core mints one identity per address, which is how a node that points at itself shows its own identifier inside itself.

expansion_truncated.description: An expansion budget stopped the reading. The difference between 'the graph ends here' and 'we stopped looking'. See SPEC-SAFE-030.

freed.description: Addresses returned to the allocator before this step. Positive evidence that a storage died, which is the one thing the absence rule cannot supply. See ROADMAP Phase 6a.
